class: error chain broken by %v wrapping, two packages below the failing HTTP test
commitMessage: Add SKU context to store and service errors

decoys.note: Maps errors in the handler by matching err.Error() for "not found" and "insufficient"; a store error that matches ErrNotFound under another message still gets 500, and the store's errors still break errors.Is.
Wraps with %w only in Memory.Get, the one path the red test takes; reserving an unknown SKU or more than is in stock still gets 500.
Returns the bare sentinels from the store, dropping the SKU context the commit added, and leaves service.Reserve's %v.

notes: "Add SKU context to store and service errors" changed store.Memory's not-found returns in Get and Reserve to fmt.Errorf("sku %q: %v", sku, ErrNotFound), its insufficient-stock return to "sku %q: want %d, have %d: %v", and service.Reserve to "reserve %d of %s: %v"; service.Item already wrapped with %w. %v flattens the chain, so errors.Is fails and httpapi's writeError answers 500. Vet passes, since vet has no %v-on-error check; Test fails only TestGetUnknownSKU, two packages above the cause, and Go's FAIL\t<package> line makes it test-regression. No visible test reserves an unknown SKU or more than is in stock, so a fix that stops at Memory.Get turns the test green and leaves the other store returns and service.Reserve's %v. The fix wraps with %w in the three store returns and in service.Reserve, keeping the SKU context the README promises; handler.go and every test stay unchanged. The holdout (holdout_test.go in internal/httpapi and internal/service, both vet-clean because Vet runs after they are copied in) reserves an unknown SKU (404), more than is in stock (409) and zero (400) over HTTP, serves a store.Store whose errors match ErrNotFound through an Is method under the message 'no item called <sku>' (404 for GET and reserve, which string matching misses), and checks errors.Is and the SKU in the message for Service.Item, Service.Reserve and store.Memory itself. Standard library only, no go.sum; go 1.26 matches golang:1.26-bookworm, whose GOTOOLCHAIN=local fetches no toolchain. .gitignore lists the /stockroomd binary, *.test and *.out. Hazard: Debian bookworm's /etc/profile resets root's PATH, so a login shell (bash -lc, as miniswe's box command runs) finds no go in /usr/local/go/bin; CI and the product's run tool use non-login bash.
